tasks.title: Bound the open-error and pods-error alerts the way the fork-error alert is bounded
acceptance: C1 measure-first (contract section E): the report quotes, from `.dir-sdlc/handruns/2026-09-30-electron-handrun/driven-report-chrome-alert-squeeze-base.json` as T1 committed it, the verdict and `control.fired` of O19 (open error) and O22 (pods error), with the reference and alert-shown title widths of at least one Pod tab for each. For each alert it bounds, it names the `file:line` in the base stylesheet that produces the measured squeeze. Architect's reading, to be confirmed or refuted: `.listError` (`src/renderer/src/pods/PodsChrome.module.css:18-24`) sets no `flex`, so a bare alert paragraph in the `.chrome` row keeps the default `0 1 auto` basis of its whole message. Each alert's criteria below apply only when its gating observation is `defect` there; otherwise they are removed by amendment before dispatch.

C2 open-error alert, zero basis on a wrapper (encodes the Gate 1 decision, `discussion.md:30`, bound it the way the fork error is bounded, and Gate 2 D5): the open-error alert's `role="alert"` element (`PodsChrome.tsx:282` at base) is no longer a direct child of `pods-chrome` but sits inside a wrapper element that is, as the fork-error `

` sits inside `.dismissible` (`PodsChrome.tsx:293-294`). The declarations that apply to that wrapper give it the fork-error row's flex, `flex: 1 1 0` (`PodsChrome.module.css:41`), and leave its `overflow` `visible` (no `overflow`, `overflow-x` or `overflow-y` declaration applies to it), so its automatic minimum width stays its min-content width. At base, the alert element is a direct child of `pods-chrome` (`PodsChrome.tsx:281-285`) and no rule applying to it sets `flex`, `flex-basis` or `flex-grow` (`:18-24`). The scored evidence is O19 in T3's fix run.

C3 open-error alert, two-line clamp (same decision): the declarations that apply to the open-error alert element include those of `.dismissible > .listError` (`PodsChrome.module.css:54-61`): `display: -webkit-box`, `-webkit-box-orient: vertical`, `-webkit-line-clamp: 2`, `max-height: var(--oc-pod-bar-height)`, `overflow: hidden` and `overflow-wrap: anywhere`. At base, none of the six applies to it. The scored evidence is O20 in T3's fix run.

C4 open-error alert, whole message available (same decision): the element carries a `title` equal to main's message verbatim. A jsdom test in `src/renderer/src/__tests__/chrome-alerts.e2e.test.tsx` fails `pods.open` with a message and asserts `alert.getAttribute('title')` equals it. At base, no `title` is set on that element (`PodsChrome.tsx:282`). The report shows the test failing before the change (red step: command and output).

C5 pods-error alert, zero basis on a wrapper (same decisions): as C2, for the pods-error alert's `role="alert"` element (`PodsChrome.tsx:309` at base, a direct child of `pods-chrome` at `:308-312`): it sits inside a wrapper child of `pods-chrome` whose applying declarations give it `flex: 1 1 0` and no `overflow`, `overflow-x` or `overflow-y`. The scored evidence is O22 in T3's fix run.
C6 pods-error alert, two-line clamp (same decision): as C3, for the pods-error alert element. The scored evidence is O23 in T3's fix run.

C7 pods-error alert, whole message available (same decision): as C4, for the pods-error alert, with the jsdom test failing `pods.list` (at base no `title` is set, `PodsChrome.tsx:309`), red step shown.

C8 DOM hooks kept (contract section A, consumed by T3), preserved and newly tested: for each of the two alerts, a jsdom test in `chrome-alerts.e2e.test.tsx` asserts `role="alert"`, `textContent` exactly the failure message, and a `firstChild` that is a `Text` node whose `data` equals it. Discrimination is shown once per alert: wrap `{openError}` (base `PodsChrome.tsx:283`), and in a separate run `{pods.error.message}` (base `:310`), in a `<span>`; run `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/__tests__/chrome-alerts.e2e.test.tsx`; quote the failure; restore. Each window is reported (what was injected, at which line, the command run under it, and that it was restored). The existing tests at `failure-paths.e2e.test.tsx:720-738` and `:853-860` still pass unmodified.

C9 regression test (encodes test discipline, Coverage: a bug fix arrives with the test that reproduces it, and a test is shown able to fail). A node-environment test, `src/renderer/src/pods/chrome-alert-layout.styles.test.ts`, reads `PodsChrome.module.css` as text after the `#?raw` import at `PodsChrome.styles.test.ts:16` and asserts, for the rule or rules that apply to each alert, the declarations C2, C3, C5 and C6 name. A stylesheet-text test is the project's route for layout that jsdom cannot lay out (`fork-ui-regression.styles.test.ts:7-13`). Demonstrated discrimination, once for each rule that carries an alert's `flex`: revert that one declaration, run `npx vitest run src/renderer/src/pods/chrome-alert-layout.styles.test.ts`, quote the failure, restore, and quote the passing run. Each window is reported.

C10 the fork-error alert is unchanged (contract section E: O21 gates only an escalation, so this session makes no `.sir/backlog.md:35` change). Every declaration that applies to `.dismissible`, to `.dismissible > .listError` and to `.chrome > :first-child` at base (`PodsChrome.module.css:39-44`, `:54-61`, `:13-16`) still applies, with the same value, and no declaration is added to any of them, including through a changed `.listError` rule. `fork-error-layout.styles.test.ts` and `fork-ui-regression.styles.test.ts`, neither in this task's `owns`, pass unmodified. Preserved, re-measured: T3's O10-O18 and O21.

C11 no token change: `src/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css` is not in this task's `owns`. A bound that needs a new or changed token is reported as an escalation, with no partial fix. Every `var(--oc-*)` the changed stylesheet uses is in the frozen TOKENS map, which `PodsChrome.styles.test.ts` checks.

C12 encodes the project frontend fragment (indexed access under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`): no added line in an owned production file uses a non-null assertion `!`, or an `as` cast, as the guard for an indexed or destructured value.
C13 no session path: `grep -c '\.sir/'` over each owned file prints 0 (`PodsChrome.tsx` and `PodsChrome.module.css` each print 0 at base 87b15e5; the two test files do not exist at base).
C14 `npm run typecheck` in the worktree exits 0 at this task's tip.

C15 `npm test` in the worktree exits 0 at this task's tip, with 0 failed files and 0 failed tests; the report gives the passed file and test counts (base: 158 files / 2554 tests, the orchestrator's probe).
